questions.question: A video player reads a file strictly front to back, so the OS reads several blocks beyond each request into the page cache; the player's next read then completes without hitting the disk. Which anticipatory technique is this?
questions.explanation: Read-ahead (prefetching) exploits sequential access: it fetches upcoming blocks before they are requested, so application reads are served from cache instead of waiting on the device.

questions.question: Requests for cylinders 10, 190, 30, and 15 arrive nearly together; before issuing them, the kernel reorders them to 10, 15, 30, 190 to cut total head travel. Which kernel component performs this reordering?
questions.explanation: The I/O (disk) scheduler sits in the block layer and sorts or merges queued requests to minimize seeks while preserving fairness and deadlines.

questions.question: An NVMe driver finds eight adjacent 4 KB writes in its queue and submits them to the device as one 32 KB command instead of eight separate ones. What is this optimization called?
questions.explanation: Write coalescing merges small adjacent writes into a single larger operation, reducing command count and per-I/O overhead at the device.

questions.question: Eight 2 TB disks are arranged as four mirrored pairs, and data is striped across the pairs so the array survives a disk loss per pair. Which RAID level is this, and how much usable capacity results?
questions.explanation: Mirroring plus striping is RAID 10 (1+0). Half of every mirrored pair is redundancy, so usable capacity is 8 x 2 TB / 2 = 8 TB.

questions.question: A database keeps its own buffer pool and wants reads to go straight from the disk controller into user memory, skipping the OS page cache entirely to avoid double-buffering. Which open mode does it request?
questions.explanation: Direct I/O (opened with O_DIRECT) bypasses kernel buffering and the page cache, moving data between the device and user buffers — right for apps that cache themselves.

questions.question: A single-threaded server must watch 500 sockets. It builds fd_set bitmasks and calls one POSIX function, passing the highest descriptor number plus one, to sleep until any socket is readable. Which function?
questions.explanation: select() multiplexes I/O readiness over fd_set bitmasks limited by nfds. poll() takes an array of pollfd instead, and epoll is a Linux-only separate API.

questions.question: A Linux service must submit thousands of async read/write operations without paying a syscall per operation, using shared submission and completion ring buffers mapped between kernel and user space. Which mechanism provides this?
questions.explanation: io_uring exposes shared SQ/CQ ring buffers so applications queue many operations and harvest completions with few or no syscalls, outperforming the older AIO interface.

questions.question: A storage controller acknowledges host writes immediately, staging them in battery-backed RAM and flushing to platter later — fast, but data would vanish on power loss without the battery. Which caching policy is this?
questions.explanation: Write-back caching reports success before durable storage is updated, gaining latency and enabling coalescing; the battery backup covers the vulnerable dirty window.

questions.question: For a transaction log where durability outranks speed, a controller acknowledges each write only after the platter confirms it — losing the chance to batch but never acknowledging early. Which caching policy is this?
questions.explanation: Write-through caching pushes data to durable storage before acknowledging, so a crash can never lose an acknowledged write — the safe but slower counterpart of write-back.

questions.question: A backup appliance notices 50 stored copies of an identical 4 KB system block and retains just one physical copy plus 50 references, reclaiming 196 KB. Which space-saving technique is this?
questions.explanation: Deduplication hashes blocks and stores each unique block once; duplicates become pointers. 49 extra copies x 4 KB = 196 KB reclaimed.

questions.question: A disk spins at 7,200 RPM. What is the average rotational latency?
questions.explanation: 7200 RPM is 120 revolutions per second, or 8.33 ms per revolution. Average latency is half a revolution: about 4.17 ms.

questions.question: The request queue is 95, 180, 34, 119, 11, 123, 62, 64 with the head at cylinder 50. Under SSTF, which request is served first?
questions.explanation: SSTF picks the pending request nearest to the head position: 62 is distance 12 from 50, versus 14 for 64, 16 for 34, and 39 for 11. The nearest is 62.

questions.question: In a five-disk RAID 5 array, how much raw capacity is consumed by parity?
questions.explanation: RAID 5 distributes one parity block per stripe, so total parity equals one disk's capacity. Usable space is four-fifths of raw.

questions.question: A driver must move 8 KB from a disk into a physical buffer at 0x240000 via a DMA controller. Before raising the start bit, what three values must it write to the controller's registers?
alternatives: Buffer address, byte count, read/write control
questions.explanation: A DMA controller needs the target memory address, the byte count, and the transfer direction (read into memory here). 8 KB = 8,192 bytes; on completion it interrupts the CPU once.

questions.question: The request queue is 98, 183, 37, 122, 14, 124, 65, 67 with the head at 53 moving toward higher cylinders; the arm never travels past the last request in a direction. What is the total head movement under C-LOOK?
questions.explanation: Serve 65, 67, 98, 122, 124, 183 going up (130 cylinders), jump straight to the lowest request 14 (169 more), then serve 14 to 37 (23): 130 + 169 + 23 = 322.

questions.question: The request queue is 98, 183, 37, 122, 14, 124, 65, 67 with the head at 53 moving toward higher cylinders on a 0-199 disk. What is the total head movement under SCAN?
questions.explanation: Serve 65, 67, 98, 122, 124, 183, then the end at 199 (146 cylinders), then reverse to 37 and 14 (185 more): 146 + 185 = 331.

questions.question: Using the same queue (98, 183, 37, 122, 14, 124, 65, 67) and head at 53 moving up on a 0-199 disk, what is the total head movement under C-SCAN?
questions.explanation: Sweep up to 199 (146), return to cylinder 0 (199), then serve 14 and 37 (37): 146 + 199 + 37 = 382 cylinders.

questions.question: A RAID 6 array is built from five 4 TB disks. How much usable capacity does it provide?
questions.explanation: RAID 6 dedicates the equivalent of two disks to dual parity, so usable capacity is (5 - 2) x 4 TB = 12 TB.

questions.question: A 15,000 RPM disk has an average seek time of 4 ms. What is its average access time (seek plus average rotational latency)?
questions.explanation: A full revolution takes 60/15,000 s = 4 ms, so average latency is 2 ms; 4 ms seek + 2 ms latency = 6 ms.

questions.question: A network card delivers 500,000 packets per second and per-interrupt overhead is saturating the CPU. Which NIC technique batches multiple packet events into fewer interrupts?
questions.explanation: Interrupt coalescing delays and groups notifications so the CPU handles many packets per interrupt, cutting per-packet overhead.
